papers.relied_on: Row 10 scores assumed the Igls consensus recommends pre-transplant C-peptide, makes C-peptide one of four criteria for grading graft function, and notes low levels are unreliable with sensitive assays and in uraemia.
papers.full_text_shows: The text says pre-transplant C-peptide should be measured fasting with a concomitant glucose (with or without stimulation) and done the same way before and after transplant; optimal and good grades need a C-peptide rise over the pre-transplant value (and >0.5 ng/mL, 0.17 nmol/L), and marginal-or-failed is decided partly by C-peptide. It says arginine- or glucagon-potentiated testing is the gold standard but not widely available, and ends by calling the classification a work in progress to be validated in prospective studies. It has no assay-level data and cites no accuracy study of its own.
papers.quote: Thus, levels of C-peptide should be measured before transplantation to determine posttransplant graft function.
papers.key_numbers: Optimal: HbA1c <=6.5%, no severe hypoglycaemia, no insulin, C-peptide above pre-transplant. Good: HbA1c <7.0%, insulin cut by >50%. Functional C-peptide >0.5 ng/mL (>0.17 nmol/L). Low-level warning: <0.3 ng/mL (<0.1 nmol/L) fasting or <0.6 ng/mL (<0.2 nmol/L) postprandial often detected despite clinical failure.
papers.role_in_work: Primary consensus source for row 10 (D3, D2, D4, D1).
papers.design: Consensus report from a 2-day IPITA/EPITA opinion-leader workshop (Igls, January 2017); expert synthesis, no systematic review stated.
papers.population_and_size: Insulin-deficient diabetes treated with pancreas or islet transplant (and future beta-cell replacement); no patient data.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide (fasting with concurrent glucose, with or without stimulated; MMTT, arginine or glucagon named as stimulation options)
papers.assay_or_platform: Not specified; notes that assay sensitivity changes how low values are read and that testing should be done the same way before and after transplant.
papers.quality_note: International consensus (IPITA/EPITA), not a guideline or label; the authors state it must be validated and refined. Supports a 3 on D3 and D1; contains no evidence that grading changes treatment.

papers.relied_on: Row 10 scores assumed the 2021 report validates Igls against CGM (n=55) and shows limits of the C-peptide criteria, and that no Igls 2.0 existed.
papers.full_text_shows: Table and text confirm the CGM finding (TIR rises 58% to 75% to 90% to 100% from failure to optimal). The authors also say the rationale for the C-peptide and insulin criteria is weaker than for the glycaemic criteria, that the 50% insulin-reduction rule is expert opinion, that the stimulated C-peptide requirement was felt too cumbersome, and that it is not known whether Igls predicts outcomes or guides decisions. They propose a preliminary Igls 2.0 in which treatment success rests on glucose metrics alone and C-peptide (absolute, not relative to baseline) only qualifies graft function.
papers.quote: It is still not known whether the Igls criteria may predict outcomes in β-cell replacement therapy
papers.key_numbers: CGM validation: 55 islet recipients, 146/36/90/30 assessments (optimal/good/marginal/failure); median TIR 100/90/75/58% vs 54% pre-transplant; TBR 0/0/2/7% vs 9% (P<0.0001). Proposed Igls 2.0: good = stimulated >0.5 ng/mL (0.17 nmol/L) or fasting >=0.2 (0.07); marginal 0.3-0.5 stimulated or 0.1 to <0.2 fasting; failure <0.3 stimulated (0.10 nmol/L) or <0.1 fasting. Centre A: treatment success about 60% of recipients in first 2 years.
papers.role_in_work: Validation and critique of the Igls criteria; evidence for row 10 D2 (cohort/validation) and D8 (added value), plus D1 and D3 context.
papers.design: IPITA symposium report (July 2019) with illustrative centre data from 4 centres and a CGM validation cohort from a fifth; no formal accuracy analysis.
papers.population_and_size: Islet, solitary pancreas and SPK recipients: centre A 36 islet, 29 pancreas, 23 SPK; centre D 10 islet recipients; CGM cohort 55 islet recipients (39 islet-alone, 16 islet-after-kidney), 1 to 10 years follow-up.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide (fasting and stimulated, MMTT) as part of a composite with HbA1c, insulin dose and hypoglycaemia; CGM is the comparator.
papers.assay_or_platform: Not stated for C-peptide; CGM blinded Medtronic MiniMed, 3 to 5 days.
papers.quality_note: Symposium report with selected centre examples; one author discloses consulting for Semma and Sernova and grant support from Xeris. Igls 2.0 is explicitly preliminary. Footnote: C-peptide may not be reliable in uraemia.

papers.relied_on: Row 10 S cited it as a TPIAT series; row 27 D2, D4 and D1 cited it as support that MMTT C-peptide is used around TPIAT and that no preoperative threshold is available.
papers.full_text_shows: A 10-patient paediatric retrospective chart review. It reports only post-operative MMTT peak C-peptide (mean 4.3 ng/mL at 1 year in 7 of 10; 3.3 ng/mL at last follow-up in 8 of 10), HbA1c and insulin dose. It has no pre-operative C-peptide, no Igls grading, no threshold and no outcome analysis of C-peptide, and nothing on the harm of missing graft decline.
papers.quote: At 1 year after TPIAT 7/10 patients had MMTT data available.
papers.key_numbers: n=10, follow-up 1-13 years (mean 6). Pre-TPIAT all 10 insulin independent. At 1 year 1 insulin independent with normal HbA1c, 7 HbA1c 5.7-6.4% (6 off insulin), 1 HbA1c 8.0% on insulin; 6 stayed off insulin, 4 on insulin. MMTT data missing in 3 of 10 at 1 year.
papers.role_in_work: Weak supporting citation: confirms that no pre-operative C-peptide use is shown (row 27 D1, D2, D4); gives no support for row 10 S.
papers.design: Single-centre retrospective chart review, descriptive; Wilcoxon and Fisher tests on small samples.
papers.population_and_size: 10 children with chronic pancreatitis after TPIAT (2007-2020), University of Minnesota surgery with follow-up in Colorado.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide, mixed-meal stimulated (peak during MMTT), post-operative only
papers.quality_note: Very small, retrospective, incomplete data, real-world follow-up with missed visits; authors list these limits. Not an Igls study.

papers.relied_on: Rows 10, 31 and 32 D4 cited it as showing that a C-peptide reference system exists but methods disagree and needed recalibration (row 31 adds that disagreement is greatest at higher concentrations).
papers.full_text_shows: The paper describes the harmonisation effort up to 2017: results differed across assays even when all were calibrated to the WHO pure standard, but serum-based secondary calibrators value-assigned by a JCTLM-listed ID-LC/MS procedure greatly reduced between-method variability. It also says the system is not complete: no serum certified reference material was listed, two listed ID-LC/MS procedures had a bias discrepancy to be resolved, and the authors propose a new reference measurement system with next steps. C-peptide is noted as an FDA-exempt assay so recalibration needs no new submission. The local text contains no concentration-specific disagreement numbers.
papers.quote: as currently no certified reference materials for C-peptide in serum are available or listed in the JCTLM database
papers.key_numbers: Uncertainty of ID-LC/MS reference procedure about 10% in the reference range; DDL procedure agreed within 5% between two laboratories; recalibration requested from manufacturers from July 2014; JCTLM listing of ID-LC/MS procedures 2014.
papers.role_in_work: Assay-standardisation evidence for D4 on rows 10, 31 and 32.
papers.design: Narrative review and position paper by the NIDDK C-peptide standardisation group and metrology institutes.
papers.population_and_size: No patients; assay methods and reference materials.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide (assay standardisation; applies to random, fasting and stimulated samples)
papers.assay_or_platform: Immunoassays in general; ID-LC/MS reference measurement procedures (NMIJ, DDL); no named commercial platforms.
papers.quality_note: Status as of 2017; whether manufacturers completed recalibration is not stated in the text. Under clarification 20 this is older-generation data, so confidence on D4 stays at medium at most.

papers.relied_on: Row 10 V2:D2 assumed this cohort validates modified Igls criteria against independent measures in TPIAT.
papers.full_text_shows: In 379 TPIAT patients (69% classifiable at 1 year) the Auto-Igls class tracked islet mass, CGM time in range 70-140 mg/dL (n=21) and the acute C-peptide response to IVGTT (n=92). It also shows a weakness of the C-peptide criterion: 23% of patients had fasting C-peptide <=0.5 ng/mL but stimulated >0.5, and 2 of 10 'failed' patients were insulin-independent with normal HbA1c, so were misclassified. The authors suggest a lower fasting threshold (below 0.2 ng/mL) when no MMTT is available.
papers.quote: 57 (23%) had fasting C-peptide ≤0.5 ng/mL but stimulated C-peptide >0.5 ng/mL
papers.key_numbers: n=379; classifiable 264 (69%); failed 10 (3.8% of classified); fasting vs stimulated discordance 57/248 (23%); TIR 70-140: optimal 81%, good 60%, marginal 44% (ANOVA p=0.02); ACRglu 15.0, 6.9, 1.4 ng/mL (p<0.0001); 41 of 258 with all four criteria (16%) downgraded to marginal by one criterion (HbA1c 26, insulin 8, severe hypoglycaemia 7). Fasting C-peptide <0.2 ng/mL consistently went with stimulated <=0.5.
papers.role_in_work: Cohort validation of an adapted Igls classification; applies to rows 10 and 27 (post-TPIAT graft function).
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre analysis of a prospective cohort, stepwise regression and one-way ANOVA.
papers.population_and_size: 379 TPIAT recipients (98 children), University of Minnesota 2010-2018; CGM subset 21, IVGTT subset 92.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide, mixed-meal stimulated (MMTT, 6 mL/kg Boost HP, 0/1/2 h) preferred, fasting as fallback; IVGTT acute C-peptide response as the validator
papers.assay_or_platform: Local or patient's own laboratory; not specified.
papers.quality_note: Retrospective, one centre; CGM and IVGTT subsets from trial participants (selection bias, authors say); 31% not classifiable mainly from missing insulin dose; Auto-Igls is an adaptation, since TPIAT has no pre-transplant baseline.

papers.relied_on: Row 10 V2:D2 and V2:D8 assumed CITR data show fasting C-peptide predicts severe-hypoglycaemia absence (AUC 0.906) and the optimal outcome (AUC 0.845, cut point 0.33 nmol/L) in 677 islet-alone recipients.
papers.full_text_shows: The numbers match. The analysis is of concurrent measures (C-peptide and outcome at the same follow-up point), uses ROC for single predictors with no other explanatory factors (so no comparison with HbA1c, insulin dose or CGM), and stimulated C-peptide reporting is sparse (44% at 1 year, 17% at 5 years) and not standardised across sites. Severe hypoglycaemia is almost eliminated even at a fasting C-peptide of 0.07 nmol/L; higher values are needed for HbA1c and insulin independence. The authors state that optimal thresholds had not previously been established.
papers.quote: In the absence of an MMTT, a fasting C-peptide ≥0.33 nmol/L is a reassuring measure of optimal islet graft function.
papers.key_numbers: n=677 of 985 islet-alone recipients (pre-transplant C-peptide <0.1 nmol/L); follow-up 4.6 +/- 1.1 years. Fasting C-peptide AUC 0.906 (severe hypoglycaemia absent, cut 0.070 nmol/L), 0.845 (optimal outcome, cut 0.33 nmol/L), lowest 0.702 (HbA1c <=6.5% and no severe hypoglycaemia). MMTT-stimulated C-peptide:glucose ratio cut 0.12 nmol/mmol; stimulated C-peptide 0.97 nmol/L for the optimal outcome. Cut points for HbA1c-based outcomes 0.31 nmol/L.
papers.role_in_work: Registry accuracy study for the C-peptide criterion in islet transplant (row 10 D2; partial D8).
papers.design: Registry analysis (CITR), ROC-AUC and optimal cut points, concurrent not prospective prediction.
papers.population_and_size: 677 islet-alone transplant recipients, US, Canada and some European and Australian centres.
papers.measure_type: C-peptide: fasting, MMTT-stimulated, and C-peptide-to-glucose ratio (fasting and stimulated)
papers.assay_or_platform: Site-specific local assays and test protocols, unstandardised (authors' own limitation).
papers.quality_note: Large registry but incomplete reporting that falls with follow-up (imputed zero C-peptide after graft loss); concurrent design; no adjustment or comparator tests; no conflicts reported. Association with outcomes, not evidence that C-peptide-guided decisions change outcomes.

papers.relied_on: Row 10 V1:D7 used 915 US pancreas transplants in 2023 as the base of its patient-count chain.
papers.full_text_shows: The 915 figure is confirmed (918 in 2022; 23 in recipients under 18). The report has new adult waiting-list additions and prevalent listings but nothing on islet transplants or on C-peptide testing. It also defines pancreas graft failure by removal, re-registration, death or insulin use >=0.5 units/kg/day for 90 days, not by C-peptide, so the assumed 50% share of new recipients graded by C-peptide has no support in this source.
papers.quote: total insulin use is greater or equal to 0.5 units/kg/day for 90 consecutive days
papers.key_numbers: 915 pancreas transplants in 2023 (918 in 2022; 12.3% below 2012). New adult listings 2023: SPK 1,585, PAK 111, PTA 180. Prevalent adult listings: SPK 3,549, PAK 370, PTA 564. Paediatric transplants 23. 1-year graft failure for 2022 transplants: PAK 15.6%, PTA 12.5%, SPK 9.2%.
papers.role_in_work: Denominator source for the D7 chain on row 10.
papers.population_and_size: US pancreas transplant candidates and recipients, 2023.
papers.measure_type: None (registry counts; graft failure defined by insulin dose, not C-peptide)
papers.quality_note: Authoritative registry; relevant only for the count, not the test. Shares used in the chain (C-peptide-graded fraction, prevalent pool) are not in the report.

papers.relied_on: Row 4: Rec 1.1 (Grade 1, moderate) recommends insulin (high-sensitivity) and fuel and hormone measures at hypoglycaemia, with insulin supportive; C-peptide and numeric thresholds in Table 1. Row 24: Rec 1.4 (Grade 1, low quality) supports an insulin and C-peptide work-up for HI after age 2 and for insulinoma or MEN1.
papers.full_text_shows: Rec 1.1 is Grade 1 with moderate-quality evidence and says insulin must be measured with a high-sensitivity assay; it also says that when insulin is elevated but ketones are high and glucagon response absent, the assay may be insensitive and the focus should be on markers of insulin action. Rec 1.4 (Grade 1, low quality) says to screen children whose HI begins after age 2 years for insulinoma; its text names no insulin or C-peptide measurement, only that insulinoma should be considered and MEN1 genetics directed accordingly. C-peptide is not mentioned anywhere in the local text, and the tables are not in the local file (the Table 1 thresholds could not be checked).
papers.quote: In children older than 2 years of age with acquired HI, the possibility of an insulinoma should be considered
papers.key_numbers: Rec 1.1: Grade 1, moderate quality (three of four circles). Rec 1.4: Grade 1, low quality (two of four circles). Newborns tested before 72 h should be retested after 72 h if hypoglycaemia persists. Glucose requirement above 8 mg/kg/min in a neonate (normal 4-6). Genetic testing PPV up to 94% for focal HI; guideline committee of 17 members.
papers.role_in_work: Primary guideline for rows 4 and 24 (D3, D2, D1, D8, D4, D5, D6, S).
papers.design: International GRADE-graded clinical practice guideline (ICPE societies), 3-year writing process with expert opinion where evidence is thin.
papers.population_and_size: Infants and children with hyperinsulinism; no patient data.
papers.measure_type: Insulin (high-sensitivity) at spontaneous or fasting-induced hypoglycaemia (critical sample), with BOHB, FFA, GH, cortisol and glucagon response; C-peptide not in the local text
papers.assay_or_platform: High-sensitivity insulin assay required; no platform named; provocative glucose, leucine or protein tests described as not useful for diagnosis.
papers.quality_note: Guideline authors are mostly paediatric endocrinologists; the committee does not list a conflict-of-interest statement in the local text. Tables and figures missing in the local copy, so numeric thresholds are not verifiable from this file.

proposals.reason: V8 scored 3 because Rec 1.4 names the age group explicitly. The full text of Rec 1.4 recommends screening for insulinoma but names no insulin or C-peptide measurement; the measurement recommendation (Rec 1.1) covers hyperinsulinism diagnosis generally and is written mostly around neonates. Under clarification 5 (condition named, not the test) and clarification 14 (broader population) this is 2. The V8 reason itself notes C-peptide is not named. Only V8 carries this dimension on row 24 among the entries cited here.
proposals.quote: In children older than 2 years of age with acquired HI, the possibility of an insulinoma should be considered

proposals.reason: V9 scored 3 on the basis that guideline text makes the test the entry step for the insulinoma path. The full text of Rec 1.4 does not name any biochemical test, and Rec 1.1 says markers of insulin action (ketones, glucagon response) should be given priority over the insulin level when they disagree. No reclassification data exist, and clarification 19 allows 3 only with data or guideline text showing the measurement changes the answer given the alternatives; mechanism alone is at most 2. V9 already marked confidence low.
proposals.quote: the focus should be on the markers of insulin action, not the insulin level itself

proposals.reason: Borderline, no change proposed. The full texts confirm consensus plus cohort validation (C068 CGM gradient, C253 n=379, C271 n=677), which fits 3 under clarification 10, but C068 states it is unknown whether Igls predicts outcomes or guides decisions, and says the C-peptide and insulin criteria have weaker rationale than the glycaemic ones. The V2 reason already records the lack of decision-impact evidence, so the abstract-level reading did not overstate. A skeptic who reads anchor D2 strictly as decision impact could argue 2; that is a reading of the anchor, not new evidence.
proposals.quote: It is still not known whether the Igls criteria may predict outcomes in β-cell replacement therapy

proposals.reason: No change. C271 compares C-peptide measures with each other, not with HbA1c, insulin dose or CGM, and C068 and C052 argue C-peptide is the only direct sign of graft secretion but give no incremental-value analysis; C253 shows the C-peptide criterion can misclassify (2 of 10 'failed' normoglycaemic off insulin). Matches the current 2 (defined subgroup).
proposals.quote: Measurement of C-peptide provides an estimate of the contribution of engrafted islets to glycemic control

proposals.reason: No change. C052 says C-peptide should be measured before transplantation and pre-transplant testing is critical, which fits a consensus recommendation in a specific population (3). It is an international consensus, not a guideline or label; C068 proposes a preliminary Igls 2.0 in which treatment success would not need C-peptide, so 4 is not supported.
proposals.quote: Thus, levels of C-peptide should be measured before transplantation to determine posttransplant graft function.

proposals.reason: No change. C224 shows harmonisation was incomplete in 2017 (no serum certified reference material listed; two reference procedures with a bias discrepancy), and C052 says testing must be done the same way before and after transplant, which supports 2 for unstandardised assays. The protocol part of the reason belongs to D5 under clarifications 16 and 25, but the assay-only score would still be at most 3, and the row 31 score for the same assay is 3; this is a consistency note for a later rescoring decision, not a change from this paper.
proposals.quote: as currently no certified reference materials for C-peptide in serum are available or listed in the JCTLM database

proposals.reason: No change. C302 confirms 915 transplants in 2023 but the share graded by C-peptide is an assumption the report does not support: US registry graft failure uses insulin dose, not C-peptide. If that share is lower than assumed (for example 10% of new recipients and of the pool) the count falls to about 900, near the bin 1/bin 2 boundary; the existing entry already marks bin 2 at low confidence.
proposals.quote: total insulin use is greater or equal to 0.5 units/kg/day for 90 consecutive days

proposals.reason: No change. Rec 1.1 is Grade 1 with moderate-quality evidence and requires insulin by a high-sensitivity assay in the critical sample, which supports 3; it is not required for the diagnosis (the text prioritises insulin-action markers when they disagree), so not 4. The V1 statement that C-peptide appears in the less definitive criteria cannot be checked in the local text (tables missing).
proposals.quote: Insulin should be measured using a high-sensitivity assay

proposals.reason: No change. The full text supports the current reading that insulin is supportive and that ketone and glucagon markers are the sensitive ones.
proposals.quote: Suppression of BOHB and preservation of a large glycemic response to glucagon are particularly sensitive markers of inappropriate insulin action.

proposals.reason: No change. C111 contains no pre-operative C-peptide and no analysis linking C-peptide to a decision; only post-operative MMTT peak values (n=10). Row 27 D1 (V24) and D4 (V22) likewise unchanged: C111 shows MMTT missing for 3 of 10 at 1 year, in line with specialist-centre use.
proposals.quote: At 1 year after TPIAT 7/10 patients had MMTT data available.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 24 (use, tests and sources columns)
claim_issues.issue: The row says insulin and C-peptide at hypoglycaemia 'as in row 4' are recommended under Rec 1.4 (Grade 1, low-quality evidence) for insulinoma and MEN1 work-up. The full text of Rec 1.4 names no insulin or C-peptide measurement; it says to screen for insulinoma in children whose HI begins after age 2 and to direct genetics for MEN1. The insulin recommendation is Rec 1.1 (Grade 1, moderate quality). C-peptide is not named in the local text of the guideline at all.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Rec 1.4 (Grade 1, low-quality evidence) recommends screening children whose hyperinsulinism begins after age 2 years for insulinoma and directing genetic work-up for MEN1; it names no biochemical test. Measurement of insulin (high-sensitivity assay) at hypoglycaemia comes from Rec 1.1 (Grade 1, moderate-quality evidence), which covers hyperinsulinism diagnosis in children generally.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 4 (caveats: 'less definitive' insulin and C-peptide criteria, thresholds)
claim_issues.issue: The thresholds (insulin >1.25 uU/mL, C-peptide >0.5 ng/mL at glucose <50 mg/dL; BOHB, FFA and glucagon cut-offs) come from Table 1, which is not in the local full-text file, and C-peptide is not mentioned in the local text. They are not contradicted but cannot be confirmed from the stored text.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Table 1 values (insulin, C-peptide, BOHB, FFA, glucagon response) are recorded from the published table (PMC11124746); the stored text copy lacks tables, so these numbers are not re-verified in the local file.

claim_issues.issue: C068 (IPITA symposium report, 2021) proposes a preliminary Igls 2.0 with absolute C-peptide thresholds (good: stimulated >0.5 ng/mL, fasting >=0.2 ng/mL) and treatment success defined by glucose metrics alone; it calls these criteria preliminary and proposes a further workshop.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: A preliminary 'Igls 2.0' is proposed in the 2021 IPITA symposium report (PMID 34061967): treatment success would rest on HbA1c or CGM metrics and severe hypoglycaemia alone, and C-peptide (absolute thresholds: stimulated >0.5 ng/mL or fasting >=0.2 ng/mL for good function) would only grade graft function. The authors call it preliminary and call for a new consensus workshop; it is not adopted.

claim_issues.issue: C111 is a 10-patient paediatric chart review reporting post-operative MMTT peak C-peptide; it has no Igls grading and Igls baseline comparison is not applicable to TPIAT. It does not support the row 10 classification of allotransplant or pancreas graft function. Better TPIAT evidence for graft grading is C253.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Remove PMID 38895780 as support for row 10 and cite it under row 27 as a descriptive series (n=10, post-operative MMTT peak C-peptide). For TPIAT, cite Auto-Igls (PMID 33020957, n=379): fasting C-peptide <=0.5 ng/mL with stimulated >0.5 ng/mL in 57 of 248 patients (23%), so fasting alone can over-call graft failure.

claim_issues.where: claims and score reasons for rows 31 and 32 D4 (and usecases text that 'a reference measurement system exists' for C-peptide)
claim_issues.issue: C224 says the reference measurement system for C-peptide was still being implemented (as of 2017): two JCTLM-listed ID-LC/MS procedures existed, but no serum certified reference material was listed, a bias discrepancy between the two procedures was being investigated, and a new system with next steps was proposed. The local text does not state that methods disagree most at higher concentrations.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: A reference measurement system for C-peptide was being implemented in 2017 (two JCTLM-listed ID-LC/MS procedures; no listed serum certified reference material); methods differed even when calibrated to the WHO standard, and recalibration to serum-based calibrators reduced between-method variability (PMID 28646033). Whether manufacturers completed recalibration is not stated in the paper.

notes: All eight papers had local text; C098 is partial (tables and figures absent, so Table 1 values could not be checked; the other seven are good). No supersedes or correction keys applied to the cited entries; V7 supersedes only U1 D7, so the V1 D7 entry on row 10 is current. Path to viability: row 10 is affected, not downgraded; the missing pieces are a reconvened Igls 2.0 consensus and prospective evidence that a graft grade changes management (C068 says this is not yet known); row 24 path may need a guideline text that names the biochemical test for insulinoma screening; rows 4, 27, 31 and 32 paths are not changed. Pointer for later: C253 is relevant to row 27 (post-TPIAT graft function, MMTT versus fasting C-peptide) though it is cited only under row 10 here. No web access used. The proposals on row 24 D3 and D8 depend on reading Rec 1.1 as neonate-weighted and Rec 1.4 as test-silent; a skeptic should check Table 1 and any supplementary text of the guideline before applying them. Tool calls used: about 29 (including reading the task file, rubric, score files, eight papers and the two output files).
